utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we ask the witness to be escorted in, I have a few matters I would like it deal with. The first is dealing with transcripts of intercepts tendered with Milan Babic. In its motion to have the evidence of Milan Babic admitted pursuant to Rule 92 quater, the Prosecution tendered a number of intercepts as associated exhibits. However, most of these end with suggested revisions to the text, and the Chamber refers, in particular, to 65 ter numbers 20101, 20112, 20131, 20183, 20244, 20250, 20253, 20296, 20298, 20351, 20405, 20411, 20464, 20483, and 20507. The Prosecution is requested to clarify who made the suggested revisions and address the reliability of such documents, in light of the suggested revisions. The Defence is also invited to set out their position on this matter. The parties should make these submissions either in court on Thursday or in writing by Friday. The second item is about documents which were MFI'd during the testimony of Ewan Brown. During the testimony of Ewan Brown, several documents were marked for identification, awaiting further submissions from the Defence. This concerns D416, D423, D431, P2900, and P2923, up to and including P2932. And perhaps the witness could already be escorted into the courtroom. Regarding D416, the Chamber expressed that it's interested the provenance of the document and whether it should be bar tabled. For D423, there was a translation issue the Defence would see to. For D4341, there was no original document available, and the Defence stated that it would sort this out. Regarding P2900 and P2923 up to and including P2932, tendered by the Prosecution, the Defence was granted further time to consider its position, and the Chamber would like to hear from the parties on these matters, and we'd perhaps do that after one of the breaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I again remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Ivetic please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you if you could tell us, did you keep a log of all the documentation and materials that you would have had occasion to look at for purposes of performing your review and analysis and in drafting the report but which you did not cite?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an overview of the search terms I used. I also -- I mean, I stored some of the documents that I didn't use for the -- but I reviewed but I didn't use for the report while I was working on the computer, and perhaps I still have that on a hard drive because I -- I had the habit of storing the work did I during the four visits I made to ICTY in order to compile this report, to store it on a hard drive in order to also work on it while I was in Lebanon. So if you want, I can show that to you, I mean, during the break or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you occasion to research beyond the documentation that the Prosecution already had in its possession to seek additional documentation by way of Requests for Assistance from any governments or any agencies?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not draft such requests or ask the Office of the Prosecutor to make such requests for this specific report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, for purposes of drafting your report in the Mladic case, you have already mentioned some books by General Kadijevic and by Presidency member Jovic as having been looked at by you. Did you have occasion to consult any of the literature out there about the intelligence cycle method of review or speak to any other experts on the topic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have had -- I mean, I attended several training courses where the intelligence cycle was discussed. I also briefly participated in a course at ICTY for criminal analysts, but I was called for other duties. And also something that is not mentioned in my CV, I teach every two, three months at the Centre of Excellence for Standing Police Units in Vicenza, Italy, on intelligence in UN peacekeeping operations, and the issue of the intelligence cycle is -- is part of that. And again, there within the UN, within I would call the community of practices of the -- of chiefs, JMAC [phoen], we discuss these kind of issues because it's obviously also the methodology we use in our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you present either your draft or final report to be reviewed by anyone for purposes of verification or revision? Peer review.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think after each visit -- each of the four visits I -- I shared my work or work product and that was a draft in various stages to the -- to, I think, Mr. Groome. But I don't remember receiving any feedback except for what I mentioned yesterday, that was I think several months after the entry of the final report into what we call -- I mean, the databases and where he said that he considered the report a fairly or very, sorry, very comprehensive. But I don't recall receiving any other feedback.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up in e-court 1D1497, I'd like to focus a bit on the intelligence cycle as we promised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now as you can see, sir, this is an article entitled: "What is Wrong with the Intelligence Cycle," and is a publication by a Arthur Hulnick, and it is within the journal "Intelligence and National Security." First of all, are you familiar with either this journal or this author within the field of intelligence gathering?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've seen the magazine before, but I'm not familiar with the author, so I'd like to see a CV before reading his article.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't think they have the CV as part of the article since it's not an expert report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I think usually there is at the end of the article -- I mean, there is this a description of who the author is and what is his practical experience because -- anyway, I let you ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to page 10 of the article and that should correlate to page 967 of the underlying publication. Looks like we need to go one more page in e-court. So I guess I'm off by a page. Yep, that's the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would like to focus on the first full paragraph from the top which reads: "The reality is that policy officials often know what they want to do even before they receive the estimate, and hope that this product will confirm in some way the wisdom of the path they have already chosen. When the estimate conflicts with their views, policy consumers may dismiss it as uninformed, useless, or even obstructionist. When it agrees with what they think they already know, then they may see it as confirming, irrelevant, or again useless. Although one would think that policy makers would want to know when they were heading in the wrong direction, this is not usually the case. Policy consumers do not welcome intelligence that is non-confirming, perhaps because the large egos that brought them into positions of power do not permit admissions of ignorance." First of all, sir, based upon your experiences performing work using the intelligence cycle, do you agree with the statements of this author?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, before answering the question I note that there are no footnotes in -- I mean, the author who I don't know makes a number of assertions. I don't know what they're based on. I mean, when I look further in the article I think it is related to the whole issue of whether or not there were weapons of mass destruction in Iraq prior to the intervention, I believe, in 2003 or the invasion. Obviously, I mean, I would -- if you really want to know more about this, I think that one standard work is by a man called, I mean, I forgot his first name but last name is Heuer. It's called "Psychology of Intelligence Analysis." You can find it on the CIA web site. And there it talks about all the difficulties, I mean, an analysts can face, also the flaws analysts can have, and he introduces the concept of intelligence to please; i.e., in some environments or in some situations it may well be the case that intelligence analysts are afraid to, quote/unquote, upset their -- their supervisors or their chiefs or their commanders and then just provide an estimate or analysis that they believe will correspond with the views of their commander. I cannot deny that I -- I think I have met one such person during my military career or during my service in peacekeeping operations, i.e., a senior official who refused to listen to negative assessments -- or assessments; I mean, predictive analysis that did not correspond with his, I would say, overly optimistic view in relation to further developments of the situation. Most of the people, I mean, almost everybody I worked for, they were interested to know in what was really the situation and what the outlook of the analysts was in order to have a constructive debate. Now irrespective of that and irrespective of that paragraph, it doesn't mention the intelligence cycle let alone put the intelligence cycle into question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in two ways, can you answer the question put by Mr. Ivetic, please. Do you agree with the author or do you disagree with the author?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with his observations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, to a certain extent, but he doesn't discuss the intelligence cycle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not a black and white situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could focus on the second-to-last paragraph of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It reads as follow, gives some of the details in relation to the weapons of mass destruction analysis that was done in relation to Iraq and it reads as follows: "Accordance to James Risen, intelligence officials in both the collection and analysis arms of CIA, as well as those in other agencies, knew the sources were poor and the conclusions wrong, but they could not fight senior managers who wanted to satisfy the political needs of the White House. Even more corrupting it appears that Secretary of Defence Rumsfeld, fearing that the --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should slow down, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "... fearing that the estimate would not support the already planned invasion of Iraq, sent his own officials, neither of them intelligence officers, to find the correct information. All these steps were perversions of the estimates process." First of all, sir, isn't it clear that we're talking about the intelligence cycle here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we're talking about, I mean, a political situation where intelligence was -- where attempts were made to use intelligence as evidence. There was -- and I'm sorry to take some time, but I think it's very misleading to use an article that discusses a very specific situation in a very specific political context to put a methodology into question where -- you know, I would invite to you look at how 99 per cent of the armies in the world work, how other organisations work, and they still stick - I mean, and the police and so on - they still stick to the intelligence analysis. It was not the process, the intelligence analysis -- excuse me, the intelligence cycle. It is not the intelligence cycle that is wrong. It is the way how it was misused to create intelligence that would support certain political conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 20 of this document, and it should correlate to page 978, or if I'm consistent in my error it will be page 21. We'll see when we get there. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on the bottom of the page which I think addresses your points that you've just made, sir. The author of this article states: "I suspect that, despite my preaching about alternatives to the traditional intelligence cycle, it will continue to be taught both inside government and elsewhere. Nonetheless, it would be encouraging to think that those so deeply wedded to the flawed concept of the intelligence cycle would, in the course of studying this volume, realise that there is an alternative to the traditional view of how intelligence works. Perhaps they might even consider it for discussion. Yet we know that people tend to look for confirming rather than disconfirming data. They will seek to defend the intelligence cycle rather than consider the alternatives. Nonetheless, the intelligence cycle is a flawed vision, and thus poor theory. One need only ask those who have toiled in the fields of intelligence." Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Hulnick's assessment of the intelligence cycle and those who operate under it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, as a -- from a generic point of view, I disagree with him. Also because he doesn't propose any alternatives. You know, if he wants to launch a debate, show some alternatives, bring some footnotes. I think he is expressing his personal views. If I have his CV, I could maybe better understand why he has such negative views and why he confuses the intelligence cycle with the way how in a specific situation intelligence, as it has been confirmed -- not confirmed, but as it has been noted by many scholars, intelligence was misused to justify certain political decisions. But to -- I mean, to -- from there to then to start putting into question intelligence cycle is for me a leap where I wonder what is the scientific or academic basis for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, I think you'll see that this article is based on the concept of end notes as many journals are. Do you recognise, in addition to the many publications by Mr. Hulnick, James Risen, Sherman Kent, Harold Greenberg, are familiar with any of these authors? James Steiner?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with Sherman Kent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: James Risen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I also see it's very Anglo Saxon. It may be very focused on a typical US situation. You know, I attended a training course in the United States where we had the privilege of being together with professionals from, let's say, the United States, and we could see some cultural differences including some differences to the approach of our work between on one hand people from United States as well as people from the rest of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we tender this article at this time as the next Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would just request more information on who this author is, what his background is. We're searching for it. Can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I will tender from the bar table, Your Honours, if that's the issue. The Prosecution ask allowed to regularly tender articles and documents without giving explanations of the authors, so I don't know what the -- what the [indiscernible] of the Defence will have to be. If have to make submissions, I'd do them in writing, Your Honours, because I obviously don't at this time have the additional information that the Prosecution is seeking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be MFI'd awaiting further submissions from the Defence. Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we were able to just quickly ascertain that he is a professor at Boston University. In that context if that's acknowledged by the Defence, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the document will be admitted. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1497 receives number D449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D449 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at another article. If we can have 1D1499 in e-court, and this is a publication of an agency of Canada's Department of National Defence, the Defence R&D Canada. Are you familiar with that institution?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- excuse me, is this an official institution or is this kind of a think-tank or?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding it's an official institution.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The -- are you familiar with the 16th International Command and Control Research and Technology Symposium held in June 2011?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 4 of this document. Ah. And if we can look at the first paragraph after introduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "The traditional intelligence cycle is a conceptual model showing how intelligence operations are conducted. It consists of four steps (direction, collection, processing, and dissemination) from defining what the decision-maker needs to know to the reception of the answer that he asked for. During the last decades many criticisms and discussions were addressed towards the intelligence cycle," and then are nine endnotes which you can look at later. But I'd like to focus on what it says here about Gregory F. Treverton in his book "Reshaping National Intelligence for an Age of Information" asserts that: "'The changes in the world that are already apparent are more than enough to require a complete reshaping of intelligence and the extension of those changes into the future of the market state will only sharpen that need.'" Are you first of all familiar with Mr. Treverton, and would you agree with the opinion that he has expressed here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with him, but I don't recall a specific article written by him. I mean, the quotation, it's -- obviously, the way how intelligence has to be done needs to be reviewed in -- in the context also -- I mean, the information revolution, the Internet, and all that -- these kind of developments. Yeah, I have no problem with that. And also the market state, that there is more and more private consultancies doing similar work, and then there is a lot of outsourcing and so on. Yeah, it makes sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could -- I think the translation is caught up with us. If we could look at the next author Mark Lowenthal and his book, intelligence: "From Secrets to Policy." And he -- it is stated here: "The intelligence cycle representation misrepresents some aspects and misses many others. First it is it overly simple. Its end to end completeness misses many of the vagaries in the process. It is also oddly uni-dimensional. A policy maker asks questions and after a few steps gets an answer. There is no feedback and the diagram does not convey that the process might not be completed in one cycle." First of all, do you know of Mr. Lowenthal and do you agree or disagree with his comments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know of Lowenthal and I even read his book, "Intelligence From Security to Policy," even if that is some time ago. But I think have you to be very careful when you read a paragraph. He is talking about the representation of the intelligence cycle; i.e., what you see, the traditional diagram with four boxes and then arrows leading from one box to the other. Obviously, that is -- that if you would confine your understanding or your attempts to understand the intelligence cycle to those four boxes and the arrows, then you will not understand how it works, then will you not understand the methodology. There has to be feedback. That is correct. There has to be -- it's not that you get a question from a policy maker or your commander and then you apply the cycle and you run back. No, there is constant interaction. The information that is it being collected will obviously influence your -- the processing, i.e., evaluation -- a colation, evaluation, analysis, integration, interpretation, those four steps will influence collection. And if you go back to the person who gave direction and you say, you know, you asked me to look into this, but, hey, have you seen this and this. Then obviously direction has to change too, and this is how in my career the intelligence cycle was applied and this is what Mr. Lowenthal identifies as feedback. So I do agree with what Lowenthal says because he doesn't attack or put into request the methodology. He puts into question the way how the methodology is represented in a simple diagram and perhaps how it has been applied by some in a bit of, I would say, too narrow -- too narrow manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at the last item on the page, it says: "In the publication of the centre of the study of intelligence of the CIA, it is stated that: '... the model omits elements and fails to capture the process accurately' and the traditional intelligence cycle model should either be redesigned to depict accurately the intended goal, or care should be taken to discuss explicitly its limitations whenever it is used." Do you agree or disagree with the same?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the specific context in which these very broad and, I mean, general statements are being made which, in my view, do not put into question the methodology but they put into question how maybe in some countries or by -- some people have applied the methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at page 9 of this article in e-court, which should correlate to page 7 of the underlying article, I'd like to focus on the second bullet point from the top. It relates to endnote 5, and I can tell that you this Canadian agency is citing to Professor Hulnick again for this assertion. And it says: "Intelligence support decision-maker rather than inform him. In 5, the author infirm the idea that the decision-makers wait for the delivery of intelligence before making decisions; they rather want intelligence to support them rather than to inform them. He explains that they often have a confirmation bias to some information and they often know what they want to do even before they receive the intelligence estimate, and hope that this product will confirm in some way the wisdom of the path they have already chosen." Do you agree or disagree with this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mentioned earlier, there are for sure decision-makers who are not waiting for the -- the estimate or the predictive analysis of their intelligence staff but who have already taken their decision, and then will be very selective in -- in using that analysis that have been -- has been provided to them. On the other hand, and again I can talk very long about this, but I don't know whether that is helpful to the Court, there was a very interesting study after the NATO bombing of Serbia and Montenegro in 1999 by an investigation commission of the United Kingdom House of Commons where they said, you know, the common view so far was that intelligence has to predict the most likely option. However, this is not the role of intelligence in the current situation. And actually the -- the role of intelligence is now to present all possible options, in particular, the worst case scenario, in order for decision-makers to -- to -- in order to avoid -- excuse me, in order to avoid that decision-makers are surprised. Obviously we are talking about two different types of decision-makers. The one in this paragraph who only -- I mean, who seems to be a bit stubborn, has already made up his or her mind; or on the other hand, the decision-maker who is open for different views. You know, that -- I think that has something -- is more related to the psychology of leadership than to the intelligence cycle. I don't see any -- any -- references or any -- any -- criticism there to the intelligence cycle. It is more an issue of the decision -- the process of decision making and how decisions are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can tell you sir that the remainder of this article talks about the literature in the community about proposals for changes in the intelligence cycle and the gathering of intelligence. Do you consider that the intelligence cycle methodology is a reliable modus for performing the type of review that did you here in the report that has been labelled as P3029, marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you contend that such a stance is widely accepted in the community of similar practitioners and experts of the intelligence cycle?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's not just an issue of practitioners and what you call experts. It is an issue of what organisations and institutions and -- teach to their intelligence analysts -- or I mean to their-intelligence personnel and how these organisations are working where indeed you see debates in relation to the methodology but overall the conclusions are that the intelligence cycle, as such, is not wrong but it's the way how we apply it and, for example, as this article shows in the paragraphs we've seen, how decision-makers are handling intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to leave the intelligence cycle now and move to another topic directly to your report. In Part 1 of your report, and it's section 3 of the same, you talk about events in 1991 through 1992 in relation to the conflict in Croatia. This at pages 113 to 181 of the hard copy that you have. I'd like to ask you some stuff -- some questions about some of that. First of all, would you agree that the SFRY armed forces, including the JNA, had an obligation under Article 240 of the SFRY constitution and Article 92 of the 1982 Law of All People's Defence to defend the country from both external and internal aggression?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the mission of the SFRY armed forces was four-fold: So to defend and protect territorial integrity, sovereignty, social order, and independence of the SFRY. So I give you the literal citation of the article because, of course, the issue of internal aggression, I think there is room for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So maintaining sovereignty, social order, and independence of SFRY in your opinion does not relate to defending against internal aggression?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my answer, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you to clarify it, sir, and answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you asked was with a question mark. In interpretation of the answer of the witness, you didn't ask him to explain that. Other phrasing would have certainly assisted the witness in understanding your question. Please proceed. The question now being clear, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if an internal aggression, quote/unquote, puts into danger -- or endangers, I'm sorry, social order, then the SFRY armed force would say have to intervene on the basis of the instructions they receive from the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at the time of the secessionist movements of the Slovenes and the Croats in 1991, did the presence of armed Croat and Slovene secessionist groups, in your opinion, constitute a threat to the sovereignty, social order, and independence of the Yugoslav state?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was for sure perceived by some as a threat to that. Now, the way how this then was transformed into orders, i.e., how the Supreme Command responded to that, I think there it's not as clear-cut as you would expect from the text of the article of the constitution and the All People's Defence law.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now have you quoted to General Kadijevic's book in your report and in your testimony. In the report, it's at pages 121 through 124 of Part 1. Did you consider looking at books written by other JNA military officers from the time-period to compare to Mr. Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, not for this report but in -- before that, when I was still working here, I looked into the works of General Sekulic, I think it was Milisav Sekulic. He published some books but he also published, I mean, various articles. I think there was -- there is also if -- a general Stojadinovic who has published a number of articles. And I'm not sure about books specifically about the conflict but for sure articles about the conflict. And overall, I think there is -- there is -- my conclusion was that there was quite some degree of consistency between the views of all these generals on one hand but also -- I mean, comparing those views, then, with the actual military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you analyse other parts of Kadijevic's book dealing with the preparations of the Croats in the period leading up to 1991 for an armed insurgency?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the entire book by General Kadijevic, but I didn't analyse those aspects because I considered that they were outside the scope of this specific report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your research reveal that he was schooled at the American -- or the US war college?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your research reveal that Mr. Kadijevic was schooled at an American institution; specifically, the US war college?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a vague recollection that he was partly trained in the United States, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And General Kadijevic himself -- declared himself to be Yugoslav, whereas his parents were of mixed Serb and Croat ethnicity. Did that come up in your research?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I -- I mean, I don't -- I didn't consider that relevant for the way how he acted as the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command and also as, obviously, the secretary for All People's Defence in the latter half of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree in terms of methodology that when one looks at a single source it generally cannot be considered reliable as to describing a situation in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is a very generic question well, like, I -- I would like to clarify the issue in my answer. In my report, I -- when I talk about General Kadijevic and his book, the section is explicitly titled -- or explicitly refers to his book, so I don't claim that this is how developments went, nor I say that this is how General Kadijevic sees or -- or considers how situation unfolded. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you chose to select General Kadijevic's book over any of the others that you read. You decided to present one position.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's also a misrepresentation. I choice Kadijevic because I have two -- I have his book, and at the same time I have his contemporaneous documents; i.e., the orders and the guide-lines he issues, in particular, during the latter half of 1991. And I could see consistency between the two. I also considered Kadijevic having been the most senior military person in the SFRY at that stage as -- as -- I would say a key player and a key actor in the context of the events we are discussing. So it's -- it's -- it's not of selecting somebody in order to ignore the work of others, but I think as I mentioned Kadijevic was a key player in -- during those times on the military level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now as for the blockades of JNA barracks and garrisons at various locations in Croatia, and this is something that you discussed last week and which is relevant to your report in Part 1, pages 113 to 181. Were all the -- were all the barracks and garrisons that are blockaded, in fact, pre-existing ones that had existed for years rather than being any type of newly established posts. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours, because I haven't conducted a detailed analysis of the blockade of all the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your research reveal and is it correct that in 1991 Croatian President Franjo Tudjman announced and called for the armed blockade of these JNA barracks and garrisons?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do recall a number of statements by -- and calls by Croatian President Tudjman. I have a vague recollection that he also made such a call in connection to the barracks, but again this was in my view outside the scope of this report, so I have not conducted a detailed analysis of this or an analysis of this in the context of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your study focus at all on the type and number of Croatian forces that were involved in the blockades of these JNA facilities as well as their armaments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because that aspect is outside the scope of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time of the blockades of these JNA units within their barracks and garrisons, would you agree that the JNA soldiers were still mostly conscripts of the various ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a -- I'm sorry, for the transcript. Yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to turn to the Vance Plan. This is something that you raised on the 5th of December at transcript page 20342 and which you also cover in your report in Part 1, pages 175 to 179. Now, in your continued direct examination on the topic, at transcript page 20344 through 45, you claim that General Mladic was contravening the demilitarisation provisions of the Vance Plan. Now, I did not note from your oral testimony whether you claim that Mr. Mladic himself had caused for these police units to be established in the first place. Can you confirm for me that General Mladic is not taking any unilateral actions to establish these police units but rather this was done pursuant to an order of the SSNO. And if I can refer you to your own report, page 179, item number 2, and I think in e-court it's page 214. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct that the SSNO issues a number of orders to, first of all, I mean, to organise and set up RSK TO units and the same for RSK MUP. And I'm just looking at footnote 581. There is also at least one order to transform JNA units in RSK TO units. So it's discussed pages 178, 179 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please remind us who the SSNO is.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the federal secretary for All People's Defence or People's Defence, sorry, and it was at the time army General Veljko Kadijevic, but I understand he was absent at regular intervals for health reasons, so at those instances he was replaced by the chief of the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, i.e., Lieutenant-General Blagoje Adzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during the same time-period is it also correct that the Croatian side was also setting up similar police units and arming them with the weapons of the TO that were in their possession?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if -- if they do it outside the UNPAs, Your Honours, there is no issue with that. The key issue is that we see that, and that's put in my report, that the Vance Plan foresees demobilization of the armed structures in the UNPAs, their demilitarisation, and then that the weapons should be put in -- in weapons storage sites, and that obviously the only forces that remain in the UNPAs, the only authorised force would be a lightly armed Serbian police force. But we see that from the JNA side or SFRY armed forces side, what remains of them, efforts are made to actually transform other units into police units including giving those police units military-style weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, now you've mixed terminology, sir. In talking about the Vance Plan you said lightly armed, and now you have said that military-style weapons were given. Isn't it correct that military-style weapons can include so-called light and heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, I don't think I mixed anything up. The Vance Plan says that the police can only have -- can only be lightly armed. That is what the Vance Plan says. What is happening in reality or what happened in reality is that the JNA gives them also other weapons or leaves other weapons behind, but they were not to be used by the police obviously. And the police or the MUP, I mean the RSK MUP, did not have such weapons before the JNA gave them to them after the agreement in relation to the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct -- is it correct that the Vance Plan neither limited the amount of police that could remain nor the quantity of weapons at their disposal, just that they be light rather than heavy weapons. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, that's what I said: A lightly armed police force. And I have seen somewhere but I don't have that in the report, that what was meant -- I mean, was meant to consist of side-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we're at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are. First I would ask that Mr. Theunens is escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted into the courtroom, I briefly deal with P03019. The Prosecution gives the information that the map currently in e-court is the unmarked version. The version annotated by the witness has been uploaded as doc ID 0048-2279-1. And that the Prosecution request that the annotated version replace the one currently in e-court, and that the Prosecution does not rely on the B/C/S text. Madam Registrar, you're hereby instructed to replace the one in e-court by the one I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then in relation to P03026, the Prosecution advises that the second page of the document in e-court is the English translation of the B/C/S text on the map, and that the Prosecution does rely on the B/C/S text on the map, and this deals with the questions the Chamber raised in relation to these two documents. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, and thank you for addressing those matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It should be correct because I read your own messages so there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By Janet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is even emphasised that the message came from Ms. Stewart, which makes it even more reliable. Mr. Theunens, we again dealt with matters unrelated to your testimony. Our apologies. Mr. Ivetic, before I invite you to continue, could you give us a time estimate as where we are approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I anticipate, as I've indicated, that I will finish sometime in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. It's appreciated that you're sticking strictly to your time-limits. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to call up in e-court Exhibit P3055.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for that, I can introduce it as the document that you had looked at in direct examination in relation to the arming or sending of arms and personnel to the RSK MUP. And according to the chart given to us by the Prosecution, this document was seized from the police administration of Sibenik-Knin in Sibenik on 16 January 2004. Can you confirm for us that this is the case or did you not know the origin of the document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I cannot testify to the specific origin of this document, but I can confirm that a number of documents concerning RSK MUP or TO were obtained from the Croatian authorities as they had seized them during military operations in the area; for example, the Operation Storm in August 1995. I myself have participated in at least one mission, I that I was in Sisak, to conduct searches in local archives in order identify documents of that type.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you personally participate in or are you aware of any efforts to contact the official archives of the JNA to provide confirmation that the text of this order is to be found among their records?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, I cannot answer the question for this specific document, but can I -- I can say that, as I mentioned also during the examination, that, for example, when I participate in interviews, documents of this type were used - I mean, interviews of senior JNA officers, witness interviews of senior JNA officers - documents of this type were used. And obviously as part of the methodology, I would also compare not only the -- the layout of the document with documents obtained from -- from other originators but also the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now looking at the text or content of this document, would you agree with me that it calls for records to be kept of the personnel and their personnel weapons that are so transferred to the police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the text of this order does not suggest any way that this process should be done secretly or clandestinely?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think maybe if we go to -- I don't know whether there's any classification of the document. I mean, it's a telex, so if we go to the end, it could be that on the original B/C/S there is a classification mentioned of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you look at the top to start with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In translation it reads: "Strictly confidential number 28-59."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that change your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean, Your Honours answered the question; i.e., it is done -- I mean, the order is strictly confidential so it's not for public domain including the instructions that are given in the document, so you could call it clandestinely if you would use that expression. But again, the information is not for the public domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But there is no suggestion in the text of the document that this should be down outside of the knowledge of the UN Protection Forces, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if the UN Protection Forces were to be informed, then they would have received the order. I don't see the UN Protection Forces being mentioned as one of the addressees. I can only see that it's strictly confidential. So the fact that it's strictly confidential I think is sufficient to indicate that the contents is not to be shared with people who have no need to know, and the United Nations Protection Forces are part of the people who have no need to know unless they would identified -- explicitly identified as an addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've probably examined many documents issued by the armed forces during this time-period. Have you ever seen a large number of them be anything other than strictly confidential in nature, according to their heading?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since they are military documents covering actually combat operations or combat-related activities, it is normal practice that they are classified because you don't want this information to fall in the hands of individuals or people or organisations who have no need to know, so the fact whether there are many documents or few documents does not have any impact on the importance of the classification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we please have up in e-court 65 ter number 03981.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can introduce this as a document which you cite in footnote 584 of your report in Part 1. Once it comes up, we'll see that it is dated the 3rd of April, 1992, such that it predates the prior document which we were just looking at. It is sent to the 2nd Military District Command --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, the document on the screen is also from the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you say it predates but it's the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Same date as the one that we just -- as the preceding document. If we could look at the first paragraph together. "Pursuant to the request submitted by the commands of the TO," and that's explained as Territorial Defence, "units of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and in order to implement a unified procedure for the transfer of real estate and materiel of JNA, Yugoslav People's Army units to the units and staffs of the TO and the R, Republic of Serbian Krajina police units in the zone of responsibility of the UN Protection Forces in Yugoslavia, we issue the following ..." And then it's a clarification and it gives certain details. Is this the order from the SSNO that we referenced earlier?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is indeed an example of an order from the SSNO concerning the -- I mean, assistance to be provided by the JNA to the local Serb TO and also MUP prior to the withdrawal or the official withdrawal of the JNA from the UNPAs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree and that -- you can have some time to look at the remainder of the text. There's only three paragraphs or four paragraphs of the same. But would you agree that again there is not any element indicating or expressing that these actions should be kept hidden from the UN Protection Forces, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, I understand -- I think you don't have a military background because otherwise you wouldn't ask the question. If the document says "military secret, strictly confidential," and the United Nations Protection Force is not explicitly identified as an addressee, well, then any person in the military will understand that this information is not to be shared with members of the United Nations Protection Force, because otherwise they would have been identified as an addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me go back to what you yourself said as an expert opinion: A subordinate needs to understand his orders that are given to them and how to carry them out. How is a subordinate supposed to know that something is supposed to be kept hidden from the UN Protection Forces if a superior does not indicate in the order keep this secret from the UN Protection Forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Ivetic, look at the classification of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how does -- how does a soldier understand what his obligations are? Would you agree that the document itself does not indicate that any soldier participating in following through this order is supposed to hide these activities from the UN Protection Forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you are asking Mr. Theunens whether this document indicates something like, You, soldier, do not share with -- this with the UNPROFOR, then it's clear the document doesn't say that. How to interpret that is a different matter. The witness has given his interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'm asking him to explain that in light of his prior testimony, that the subordinate needs to know precisely the orders of his superior. How is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One would be inclined to understand that every soldier would know that the document which starts with @military secret, strictly confidential," should not be shared with any outsider. That it would be the common understanding without saying, You, Soldier, don't give it to UNPROFOR, don't give it to NATO, don't give it to the Polish army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, my point is not about the document. It's about the activities described in the document; the transferring of people and weapons to particular locations. That is not in relation to the document. It's something that can be observed by outside people. And in the military, in every single military that I've ever studied, if there's camouflage that's meant to be applied, it has to be set forth in an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your question then is where, in this order, no specific measures are prescribed for keeping the activities confidential, how does this fit into your position that subordinate military staff should always receive clear instructions as to how to perform their tasks. That's the question then, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And tagged with his other testimony that this activity was a contravention of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. Your Honour, starting with the last element, the fact that it is a contravention or actually a circumventing of the demilitarisation clause of the Vance Plan is explained in footnote 587 in Part 2 of the report, which is based on -- which comes from reports by the UN Secretary-General on the implementation of Security Council Resolution 743 that explicitly deals with how the UN forces were implementing the Vance Plan. Returning to document. When you look at the bottom at the addressees, it is addressed to the Command of the 1st Military District and the command of the 2nd Military District. It is not addressed to individual soldiers. As you have explained in the beginning, when we reviewed the principles of command and control, the various commanders throughout the chain of command will develop detailed instructions for their subordinate personnel in order to implement this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, if we can have this document admitted as the next Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection. And for the record, the Prosecution received this document from the BiH Ministry of Defence on 1 September, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03981 receives number D450, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have a look at 65 ter number 726 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think this give us a better picture of where General Mladic stood in relation to the Vance Plan and its success. It is also a document that's on the chart of documents used by you but is identified as not being tendered. If we -- it is dated after the Vance Plan based upon the fact that it references the same. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think if avoided extraneous comments. This was a document that we originally indicated that we would want to have a pre-Chamber guidance, so I just wanted to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You made that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the first paragraph, we see that it's talking about the Vance Plan, the agreement are reached between Mr. Vance and various people on 2nd January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the bottom of the page in Serbian and the top of the next page. And in the bottom the second -- in the English this is the bottom of the second page and bleeds onto the top of the third.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please remind me of the date of this document, because I haven't been able to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if we go back -- if you look at the Serbian original, it dates sometime after the 2nd of January 1992. I agree that there is not a date visible on the document, nor I believe also on -- on the last page there is not a date.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you look at this page that we're looking at, in the English they say this agreement came into effect in application at 1800 hours local time on the 3rd of January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So it's clear it dates after that date but the specific date we may not know. If we look at this section now at the bottom of the page in English: "This agreement derives from the proposal of the SFRY, Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, Presidency, dated 9 November 1991, to the UN Security Council to urgently send UN peacekeeping forces in order to protect citizens in the Territory of Croatia with Serbian majority, and the condition set for sending peacekeeping forces is absolute and permanent cease-fire. "According to the proposed concept, UN peacekeeping forces would be deployed in areas of administrative borders of Croatia, which are behind the line of contact at the moment of cease-fire; i.e., in the areas of Krajina, Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and Western Slavonia. "These areas would be demilitarised and 'protected United Nations areas' out of range of any armed forces, except the UN forces, which would provide full physical protection of the population together with the local police. Regional and local police forces in these areas would be kept, and weapons of the disbanded paramilitary formations would be turned over to the JNA, Yugoslavs People's Army, or placed in storage in that territory, under joint control of the local authorities and UN forces." Sir, so far, does this accord with your understanding of the so-called Vance Plan? Are we talking about the same plan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, when he -- if he means by disbanded paramilitary formations RSK TO, then indeed this corresponds with the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can continue the second-to-last-paragraph on what is page 3 of the English: "The existing regional and local organs would be the governing bodies in the freed territories. The UN forces would monitor if citizens are treated equally by the police and their presence and authority of a world organisation would prevent attacks by armed forces and threats to the population in these territories." So far, sir, would you agree with me that there's nothing in this text that we've read thus far can be considered as seeking to have the Vance Plan not honoured or violated by the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is -- I would agree with that interpretation of this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in English. And at the top of the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, one moment. If we can -- if we could scroll up. I apologise. We have the first half of the page I think is not there, or is this perhaps a different translation. I apologise. If we can go back to the tail-end of the last page. We were missing some text. It's the last paragraph on this page and we'll bleed over onto the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, this is what General Mladic has written: "Sending of UN peacekeeping forces would ensure permanent cessation of armed conflicts in the territory of Croatia, prevent the spreading of armed conflicts to other areas in Yugoslavia, and offer guarantees to the Serbian people in Croatia that the Ustasha genocide against them would not be repeated. Thus the necessary prerequisites would be created to resolve the Yugoslav crisis by political means in a peaceful and just way, which is in the interest of all our peoples. "In the existing circumstances, any other orientation would obviously lead to war, with unpredictable course, duration, outcome, and consequences, and with real possibility of spreading outside of the area of Yugoslavia, which is the goal of the present government in Croatia, and Germany also aspires to that. "The engagement of UN peacekeeping forces would crucially contribute to the achievement of goals supported by the peoples living in Yugoslavia. It is therefore also in the interest of the JNA. "This is the only possible way to provide the necessary political, diplomatic, economic, and other support to preserve Yugoslavia and prevent the destructive plans of a group of EU countries. "The most important task at this point is to establish peace, consistently observe cease-fire agreements and other obligations assumed in The Hague and Geneva, and make it possible for the UN peacekeeping forces to arrive, so the Yugoslav crisis would be resolved without dictate, threat of sanctions, or further bloodshed." Sir, would you agree with me that General Mladic here seems to be supporting the UN peacekeeping option and the Vance Plan rather than trying to subvert it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. But as, I think, throughout my testimony, I've tried to show that one has to be careful in drawing conclusions just focusing on one document. In footnote 585 of Part 1 of the report, you can see a series of documents from the 9th Corps, i.e., signed by General Mladic or a member of the command of the 9th Corps, covering the February to April 1992 time-period which indicate that, notwithstanding these apparently good intentions or positive intentions of General Mladic at the time of this documents -- document, afterwards the 9th Corps indeed transfers weapons, personnel, and so on to the RSK MUP, I mean, RSK TO, RSK MUP, and contributes to circumventing the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we try to -- if I understand you well, Mr. Ivetic, you say this document shows the intentions and is fully in accordance with the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The testimony of the witness is what was done in practice is not consistent with the Vance Plan, and therefore may I take it that you consider this document to be incomplete because it doesn't mention the transfer of people and equipment to the MUP? In that respect, that it does not reflect being a report. What actually happened and where the Vance Plan say that the police force should be kept, it was, as I understand you well, enlarged considerably with the assistance of the 9th Corps. That, I think, clearly now before reading the whole of the document again, that is apparently what keeps the Defence and the witness apart. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, then I will not continue reading the document but would rather tender the document at this time so it can be read by the parties and then submissions made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection. Prosecution received the document from the Croatian state archives on 20 October 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 726 receives number D451, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D451 is admitted.

utterances.text: To do so, I would call up 1D1489, which I introduce as a part of the Karadzic transcript of proceedings. And if we could please have page 61 of the same, that should correlate to transcript page 16899 of the underlying transcript.

utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we need to correct the record a little bit because I -- when discussing crimes in the AO of 9th Corps, we spoke about crimes allegedly committed, I mean in Skabrnja and Nadin, which involved, as the documents show, units that were part or operating under the command of the local Serb TO, which in its turn was under the command of the 9th Corps. utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Isn't Arkan mentioned specifically in relation to the Skabrnja saying that the only -- that there was a reference that some officers of the JNA spoke approvingly of Arkan? Did you not write those words, sir? In the same section.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless you can show me in the report where I did it, but this is not in relation to Skabrnja. This is in relation to Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So there is mention of Arkan in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'm trying to say, it is not in the area of the 9th Corps in 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly make pauses between questions and answers, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In relation to Arkan in the SBWS, and I believe you mention them in your direct examination, I would like to look at what starts at line 2 of this transcript and proceed through line 18. Again, you can follow along while I recite for the record the answers, and then I'll have some additional questions. "Q. And in paragraph 4 of the same page, there's a reference also -- what does he state about the behaviour of Arkan's troops towards local Muslim population in Sanski Most?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.text: Your Honour, before we get too far into this, I don't know if Mr. Theunens recalls what the document that's being discussed at this time in the Karadzic testimony. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I'm stuck with the fact that there was a different report in the Karadzic case, so I was hoping that the -- that the witness would remember his own testamentary relating to Arkan specifically relating to Mr. Mladic. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We could explore whether the witness knows. If not, you should try to find out, Mr. Ivetic. Apart from that, you referred to the -- Arkan in the SBWS to have been mentioned in the direction, may I take it in this case?

utterances.text: In this case, correct.

utterances.text: Would you have a transcript reference for me?

utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that is what the letter states. I mean, the letter General Arkan sends to Mr. Karadzic as well as to the RS minister of the interior on the 23rd of September 1995, as is discussed in pages 380 to 382 of Part 2 two of my report.

utterances.text: Yes. And that is only --

utterances.text: -- the Sanski Most area.

utterances.text: That is Sanski Most exclusively, so we forget about Skabrnja --

utterances.text: -- and Nadin. We forget about SBWS. You refer to that after you mentioned the Croatian villages.

utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.text: And we now exclusively are dealing with Arkan, Sanski Most, September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.text: Starting at line 19: "Q. The view that General Mladic has here on this particular group, paramilitary group, did you see this reflected in other military documentation as well? I mean not just Arkan, but other volunteer and paramilitary groups, do you know whether they also have a quite critical view on those [sic] troops? "A. Yes, Your Honours. There is the report General Tolimir compiles on 28th of July, 1992, on paramilitary groups. In this report, Tolimir, as assistant commander for intelligence and security, shares with President Karadzic as well as General Mladic and other senior military officers, I mean members of the Main Staff, includes a very critical view, a very negative view, of various paramilitary, i.e., volunteer, groups operating on the territory controlled by the Bosnian Serbs. It talks about their lack of combat value, their -- the fact that they are inclined or prone to commit crimes against Serbs and non-Serbs. And this Tolimir report is then used as a basis for orders issued by the Main Staff to subordinate or remove these volunteers. There's also an order - and I think it's even from earlier, it is from May or June 1992 - by Mr. Karadzic as President of the Presidency of the SRBiH to subordinate these groups to the VRS or have them removed."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by this testimony as being truthful and accurate as to the matters contained therein?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do Your Honours. And the Tolimir order as well as the -- excuse me, the Tolimir report and the subsequent order by General Mladic are mentioned in Part 2 of my report. I was just trying to identify the section.

utterances.text: If we could call up Exhibit P501 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can introduce this as an order dated 28 July 1992 and is issued for the disarmament of paramilitaries --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- from the Main Staff and General Mladic. Did you have occasion to review this document for purposes of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It -- it is discussed in footnote 291 of Part 2 of the report. And prior to that, I have a detailed discussion of the Tolimir report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at the bottom of page 1 in the English, going onto page -- oops. If we could scroll down. If we can go to page 2 of both versions of the report -- of the document, it is the bottom of page 2 in the English. It's going to be the previous page in the B/C/S. I see we seem to have a problem with the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's see if I can follow along with the English. The order states in number 1: "All paramilitary formations and their leaders, if their intentions truly are honourable, are to place themselves in the service of the just struggle for the survival of the Serbian people, and are to offer to incorporate themselves into regular SRBiH army units, to be deployed in accordance with their military specialities and level of military training."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Individuals and groups which had carried out crimes, looting, and other types of criminal acts are not to be included into units. They are to be disarmed, arrested, and criminal proceedings are to be initiated against them in SRBiH army courts, regardless of their citizenship." Number 3: "Paramilitary formations, groups, and individuals which refuse to be placed under unified SRBiH army command, are to be disarmed and arrested, in co-operation with the MUP, Ministry of Interior, and criminal proceedings are to be initiated against them for crimes committed. "4. Citizens of FR Yugoslavia who accept the unified SRBiH command are to be treated as volunteers and deployed to units at the front. Those who refuse, and have not as yet committed any crimes, are to be disarmed and handed over, under escort, to the relevant FRY military and territorial organs. "5. I forbid all paramilitary formations, groups, and individuals in the SRBiH territory. In the future, criminal proceedings will be conducted against commanders, relevant military and territorial organs, and authorities who allow paramilitary organisation and evasion of recruitment and conscription in accordance with the SRBiH Law on the Army." Sir, do you agree with me that everything in this order by General Mladic is proper and is the type that one would expect of a military commander who is adhering to appropriate conduct of war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the order is very clear. Whether it's appropriate or not, that is not up to me to say that. But the order is clear. Now, from an analytical point of view, the next step would then be to look at the degree of implementation of that order, and there I would like to draw the Court's attention to the situation as it was, for example, in Sarajevo which is discussed on pages 177 and following of Part 2 of the report where we still see volunteer groups affiliated with the Serbian radical party being active there. Some of them are regularised by giving them a VRS military post number, but others continue to act as, yeah, almost independent groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the incident we just looked at in Sanski Most, where even as of 1995 Arkan's group is there and General Mladic is continuing to beg other authorities to deal with them, wouldn't that show that General Mladic did not have control over these units and an ability to get rid of them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honours. And I mean, there is more than three years between the two documents we are discussing. We are discussing an order from July 1992 and then a letter from September 1995, whereby I think it's also important to look again at the contents of the letter. General Mladic clearly spoke about loyal Muslims, and that expression, we have also discussed that during my examination, is I think quite important in order to understand his attitude towards non-Serbs. Secondly, the letter of September 1995 also has to be seen in the context of the -- I would say political conflict that opposes General Mladic to President Karadzic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is already in evidence so I do not need to tender it. And I see now that we have the B/C/S page that was missing earlier, so I don't have any suggestions as to this document. I'd like to move on.
